assumptions: Clocked at 100 MHz
Active-low reset
Valid-ready handshake for all streams
Inputs and output are 8-bit
Accumulator saturates? No, wraps modulo 256

control_flow.name: in0_buffer_load
control_flow.effects: skid_buf0_data = top.in0_data; skid_buf0_valid = 1

control_flow.name: in1_buffer_load
control_flow.effects: skid_buf1_data = top.in1_data; skid_buf1_valid = 1

control_flow.name: join_handshake
control_flow.effects: join.data_out = skid_buf0_data + skid_buf1_data; join.valid_out = 1; skid_buf0_valid = 0; skid_buf1_valid = 0

control_flow.name: accumulator_load
control_flow.effects: accum_reg = accum_reg + join.data_out; accum_valid = 1; join.valid_out = 0

control_flow.name: out_stage_load
control_flow.effects: out_stage_data = accum_reg; out_stage_valid = 1; accum_valid = 0

control_flow.name: top_output_handshake
control_flow.effects: top.out_valid = 1; out_stage_valid = 0

control_flow.name: join_fsm_idle_to_wait
control_flow.effects: join_fsm = WAIT_BOTH

control_flow.name: join_fsm_wait_to_output
control_flow.effects: join_fsm = OUTPUT

control_flow.name: join_fsm_output_to_idle
control_flow.effects: join_fsm = IDLE

requirement: Build an 8-bit event-counting subsystem as a complete SR2FPGA Verilog RTL project. This is component topology t1_event_counter, difficulty tier T1. Use an event_gate in front of a counter_core. The design must implement this black-box behavior: event_valid pulses pass through an event gate and increment the counter core. Keep rtl/top.v as the integration wrapper and keep each reusable component in a separate RTL file. Preserve these interface contracts: top.event_valid -> event_gate.event_valid; event_gate.count_en -> counter_core.en; counter_core.count -> top.count. Include system_his.json, manifest.json, timing constraints, predicted QoR, and a bounded self-checking testbench that prints TEST_PASS only on success or TEST_FAIL on failure.

system_his.description: 8-bit event counting subsystem with event gate and counter core

Keep rtl/top.v as the integration wrapper and keep each reusable component in a separate RTL file. Preserve these interface contracts: top.in_valid -> skid_buffer.in_valid; top.in_data -> skid_buffer.in_data; skid_buffer.out_valid -> accumulator_core.sample_valid; skid_buffer.out_data -> accumulator_core.sample; accumulator_core.sample_ready -> skid_buffer.out_ready; accumulator_core.sum -> top.sum. Include system_his.json, manifest.json, timing constraints, predicted QoR, and a bounded self-checking testbench that prints TEST_PASS only on success or TEST_FAIL on failure.
